docs.purpose: When someone deletes their account, the data is not removed immediately — it is marked as deleted and kept for a 30-day grace period. This job runs daily to finish the job: it permanently removes every account whose grace period has expired, one account at a time. Accounts that cannot be removed because they authored admin audit records are deliberately skipped and reported, so a human can scrub them by hand rather than the whole sweep failing.
docs.data_story: It reads `user_profiles` and writes `auth.users` and `pipeline_runs`. It runs on `0 10 * * *`, unattended, with nobody watching — which is why its guard matters: pg_extension guard with a NOTICE-skip on the cron.schedule call only (migrations/233:78-81); the `public.offboarding_sweep_30day()` FUNCTION itself is created UNGUARDED so CI/Docker images without pg_cron can still test it. Function is SECURITY DEFINER with `SET search_path = pg_catalog` and REVOKE ALL from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **JOB descriptor** of archetype `SCHEDULED` under its own `job.schema.json` (Spec 128 R-14) — declaring its schedule, its target, its idempotency posture, its behaviour when `pg_cron` is absent, and the audit row it writes. Nothing about how it runs changes; what changes is that those five answers stop living only in SQL and YAML.

inputs.why: It reads one predicate off user_profiles — the accounts whose self-deletion passed the 30-day horizon — and nothing else; no contract, no parameter.

outputs.why: NOT ANSWERABLE from the closed set: outputs offers none | contract_only | optimistic_then_contract | device_only, all of which describe a client writing through an API. This job writes directly to the database with no contract in between. The substance is recorded in outputs.tables[]; the vocabulary gap is a Spec 128 §4 escalation (R-14: JOBs need job.schema.json). What it does: a per-user DELETE FROM auth.users, whose mig-229 CASCADE topology removes every user-owned row, plus one pipeline_runs summary row at the end.

evidence: scripts/lib/step/ledger.js:62 — the SDK insert this mirrors

state.why: Three loop-local variables (deleted, skipped, skipped_ids) live for one execution; the horizon is recomputed from NOW() each run, so nothing carries over.

session.why: NOT ANSWERABLE from the closed set: guards.session offers anon | authenticated | entitled | admin, all of which describe an end-user principal. This runs with no request and no user — as the pg_cron job owner through a SECURITY DEFINER function, or as a GitHub Actions runner holding repository secrets. Spec 128 §4 escalation (Spec 128 R-14 already anticipates JOBs getting their own job.schema.json); recorded rather than mis-answered.

rls_class.why: user_profiles is a Class A uid table (auth.uid() = user_id) and auth.users is its owner; the function is SECURITY DEFINER with search_path = pg_catalog, so it runs above both policies and is REVOKEd from anon and authenticated.

checks.why: The loop must survive one bad user: the mig-229 admin_audit_log RESTRICT fence would abort a batch DELETE entirely, and the WHEN OTHERS arm 235 added covers every other single-row failure — without both, one audit-authoring account blocks every other eligible deletion.

The pipeline_runs row carrying deleted_count, skipped_count and skipped_user_ids is the ONLY durable record of a run — cron.job_run_details does not capture the RAISE WARNINGs under default config, so losing this insert makes the sweep invisible.

SET search_path = pg_catalog with every reference schema-qualified means an unqualified name is a hard error at CREATE time rather than a silent hijack risk at call time — 235 tightened this from 233 deliberately.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_profiles WHERE account_deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND account_deleted_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '31 days'
invariants.why: A day of slack past the 30-day horizon absorbs the daily cadence; a count that keeps growing means either the schedule is not firing or every remaining row is stuck behind the audit-log RESTRICT fence and needs the manual RTBF scrub.

errors.why: A JOB has no UI, so `envelope` is read here as its structured-record analogue: per-row, inside the loop, a foreign_key_violation (the audit fence) and any other error are each caught, RAISE WARNING'd with the user id, counted as skipped and recorded in skipped_user_ids on the pipeline_runs row — the batch continues either way.

classes.ui: RAISE WARNING plus a skipped_user_ids entry on the pipeline_runs summary row; the sweep continues

emits.why: One pipeline_runs row per run, pipeline='offboarding_sweep', status='completed', carrying deleted_count, skipped_count and skipped_user_ids — added by 235 precisely because RAISE WARNING is not durable.
breadcrumbs: RAISE WARNING 'offboarding_sweep_30day: user % skipped — admin_audit_log RESTRICT fence'
RAISE WARNING 'offboarding_sweep_30day: unexpected error for user %'

offers.why: A deletion sweep renders no sponsored placement.

metering.why: It writes no usage_events row; the counts it reports go to pipeline_runs, not to the usage ledger.

config.why: The 30-day horizon is a literal INTERVAL in the function body, not a registered logic variable — unlike the sibling purge, whose window IS tunable. That asymmetry is measured, not assumed.

limitations.what: A user who ever authored an admin_audit_log row is never deleted by this job.
limitations.measured: migrations/235_offboarding_sweep_hardening.sql:69-76 — the foreign_key_violation arm skips them and leaves them for a manual RTBF scrub; migration 229 makes admin_audit_log.admin_uid ON DELETE RESTRICT on purpose, so an audit trail outlives the account that wrote it.

limitations.what: The retention horizon cannot be changed without a migration.
limitations.measured: migrations/235_offboarding_sweep_hardening.sql:61 — INTERVAL '30 days' is a literal in the function body and appears nowhere in docs/reference/logic-variables-registry.md.

notes: Scheduled once in 233 (`0 10 * * *`); 235 replaces the function body only (CREATE OR REPLACE) and does NOT re-schedule this job. 235 adds a `WHEN OTHERS` per-user exception arm and a durable `pipeline_runs` summary row (pipeline='offboarding_sweep', status='completed', records_meta carrying deleted_count/skipped_count/skipped_user_ids) because pg_cron's job_run_details does not capture RAISE WARNING output. The auth.users DELETE cascades across the mig-229 topology; admin_audit_log is ON DELETE RESTRICT by design. MEASURED 2026-09-15. This is the catalog's best-instrumented job and the one the other two should be measured against: it is the only pg_cron job with a live DB test (src/tests/db/offboarding-sweep.db.test.ts) and one of two that write a pipeline_runs row. Its 30-day horizon is a literal while the sibling purge's window is a registered logic variable — a real asymmetry, recorded in config.why rather than smoothed over. guards.session and outputs.answer are Spec 128 §4 vocabulary escalations; outputs.tables[] carries the substance, including auth.users, which is the only cross-schema write in this shard.
